subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — pricing/tenor options & buyer approval path
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer: term length and pricing for AWS Marketplace listing

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get concrete pricing/term options we can take to finance and the CFO. Two items they care about: a) whether we do a 1-year annual commit vs a 2/3-year locked term (they prefer multi-year if unit price is attractive), and b) what the buyer approval path and timeline looks like on the AWS private offer (our legal wants to know how quickly the offer can be routed for signature after commercial terms are agreed).

Can you send: a simple pricing grid (annual/2yr/3yr with discounts and expected activation timeline), the buyer approver matrix (who signs/typical CFO windows), and any evidence package they can use for procurement?

We want to present to our CFO (Steve Harper) on Friday; ideally we have something by EOD Thursday (PST).

Thanks — Marta
Marta Ruiz
Director, Cloud Procurement
Skyline Health

[Attachment: skyline_procurement_requirements.pdf]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: term length and pricing for AWS Marketplace listing

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a compact pricing grid that shows list vs private-offer pricing at 1/2/3 year tenors plus the activation & evidence checklist we usually hand to buyers. Key notes up front: 

- 1-year: smallest upfront, standard onboarding cadence, pricing = baseline list price with 5% usage-based discount if commit > $250k/yr.
- 2-year: ~12% effective discount vs list (phased billing options available), recommended for buyers who want fixed unit economics — AWS private offer provisioning typically goes live within 2 business days after PO + DocuSign activation.
- 3-year: ~18% effective discount with annual reconciliation; requires CFO signoff on multi-year spend and finance to accept 60–90 day invoicing window.

Buyer approval path (high level):
1) Procurement presents private offer + pricing to Finance/CFO -> 3–7 business days for standard buyers.
2) For multi-division customers (like Skyline), expect cross-BU CFO review and an extra 7–10 business days.
3) AWS private offer activation: once signed, AWS takes ~24–48 hours to enable in buyer console; we can expedite with marketplace ops if needed.

I've attached: redwood_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx and a short evidence pack excerpt. Ben — can you confirm whether we can offer 60-day invoice terms on the 3-year option (we'd need finance approval). Jonas — tagging you for co-sell signal and marketplace activation lead.

Proposed next step: 30-minute run-through with procurement + CFO tomorrow at 10am PT if that works.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx]

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Steve Harper <steve.harper@skylinehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: term length and pricing for AWS Marketplace listing

Thanks Sofia — the grid is exactly what procurement needed. Steve (CFO) asked me to confirm two things before the call:

1) If we pick 3-year with 60-day invoicing, what credit/escrow or early-termination safeguards do you require?
2) Will AWS Marketplace allow us to approve the private offer and have it visible to our billing/account team immediately after signature, or is there any delay that would impact month-end close?

We can do the 10am PT slot tomorrow. I've attached the procurement packet (their standard requirement list).

Marta

[Attachment: skyline_procurement_requirements.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinehealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: term length and pricing for AWS Marketplace listing

Marta / team — quick answers ahead of the call:

- 60-day invoicing on 3-year: possible but requires finance approver (Neha tagging). We'll need a short payment guarantee (standard is a 6-month rolling prepay or an escrow arrangement). If Skyline can agree to annual invoicing in advance, we can avoid escrow.
- AWS visibility: once the private offer is signed by both parties and we push activation, AWS typically marks the offer active in the buyer console within 24 hours. For month-end concerns, we can coordinate activation to fall prior to your close; we'll route through AWS ops to minimize latency.
- Early-termination / credit: we propose a pro-rated refund for unused committed credits with a 60-day notice clause; specifics can live in the term sheet (attached sample).

Action items:
- Sofia: confirm which tenor you want to present (1/2/3).
- Marta/Steve: provide preferred invoicing cadence (annual, quarterly, 60-day).
- Neha: please confirm finance stance on escrow vs annual prepay for this buyer profile.

I'll prepare a short mutual action plan and a DocuSign-ready term sheet after the call.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: mop_signed_term_sheet.pdf]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: term length and pricing for AWS Marketplace listing

Ben / Sofia — following up from today's call notes: 

- Skyline prefers 3-year from a TCO perspective but will only accept 60-day invoicing if we accept an escrow arrangement or provide a limited credit facility.
- Procurement asked Redwood to propose a short approval matrix showing who at Skyline signs at thresholds > $1M/year (Procurement -> BU CFO -> Corporate CFO). I've drafted a one-page approver matrix and attached it to the HubSpot deal.
- Action: Neha, can finance confirm whether we will accept escrow + deferred payment for strategic healthcare customers? If not, we should push annual-in-advance for the 3-year and offer an extra 1.5% discount as a concession.

I'll open the Marketplace private offer once terms are agreed; timeline to activate = 24–48 hours after DocuSign completion.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
